cause.what: side_memory_seconds is set to 0.0, disabling the hazard memory for wall returns near the body

evidence.shows: The purple box is already touching the robot on screen at its side, while its feet are still -81.4 px from the base's far edge, i.e. this is a side/edge obstacle, not a centred obstacle straight ahead.
evidence.value: gap 2.0 px, feet past base edge -81.4 px

evidence.shows: First real contact: the box is close to the robot's left side and partially in front of it, confirming contact with an object at the edge of the robot rather than in the middle of its path.
evidence.value: gap 1.0 px, feet past base edge -9.2 px

evidence.shows: The brain never left forward, never braked or turned, and kept commanding vx=0.24 right through contact, so the obstacle never entered the view the forward state acts on.
evidence.value: state=forward, cmd=move, vx=0.24 for every tick

evidence.shows: Just before contact the close object is only in the outermost left column (68-70 cm in rows 3-4, 101-109 cm in rows 0-2) while columns 1 onward are 101 cm or more; the central wall analysis therefore sees a clear way.
At contact the same pattern holds: column 0 reads 62-67 cm while column 1 reads 107-112 cm, so the object stayed in the edge column the whole time.
Depth frames kept arriving (new-frame marks throughout) and safe=yes throughout, so this was not a sensor-dropout, fall or health hold.
evidence.value: safe=yes on every tick, fresh frames marked '*' regularly

ruled_out.because: The brain stayed in forward with vx=0.24 on every tick from t=8.217 to t=11.424 and no brake/turn state ever appears; also the central columns in the full frames at t=11.123 and t=11.223 read over 1 m, never under the stop distance.
ruled_out.cause: A centred wall obstacle that the forward/brake logic saw but handled too late

ruled_out.because: safe=yes on every log tick and new depth frames are marked arriving throughout, up to and past contact at t=11.202.
ruled_out.cause: A fall, unhealthy robot, or missing depth frames causing a hold or blindness

ruled_out.because: The close return appears in the top and middle sensor rows too (rows 0-4 in column 0 at t=11.223), not only in the bottom floor rows, and it persists across frames 10.722 to 11.223 rather than flickering once.
ruled_out.cause: A low floor-level object or a single noisy depth zone

ruled_out.because: The outermost-column returns would have been eligible for the side-hazard memory (within its forward and sideways band); what removed them was the zero retention setting, not the central-column window, which is a deliberate design split between the two mechanisms.
ruled_out.cause: The central front columns (1-6) excluding column 0, on its own

fix_direction: Give the near-body side memory a positive retention time (as in the built-in defaults) so wall returns seen in the outer columns are kept and fed into the view ahead, then re-run this recording to confirm the robot steers or stops before the box.
explanation: The box approached at the very edge of the depth sensor's view, beside the robot rather than in the centre of its path, so the ordinary check of what lies directly ahead stayed clear and the robot kept walking. A separate safeguard exists that remembers nearby surfaces seen at the sides, but that memory was switched off in the settings, so those edge sightings left no trace and were never acted on.

plain.robot: Its log showed it kept walking forward throughout.
plain.why: It was set to forget nearby objects at its sides.
